front_question: What is the definition, SI unit/notation, and application of 'Solar Eclipse Alignment'?
back_answer:
Definition: Sun --- Moon --- Earth (Moon obstructs solar light).
Unit/Notation: New Moon Alignment
Application: Daytime solar obstruction.

front_question: What is the definition, SI unit/notation, and application of 'Lunar Eclipse Alignment'?
back_answer:
Definition: Sun --- Earth --- Moon (Earth obstructs light reaching Moon).
Unit/Notation: Full Moon Alignment
Application: Nighttime lunar darkening.

front_question: Why do we always see the same side/face of the Moon from Earth?
back_answer: The Moon's rotation period on its own axis exactly equals its orbital revolution period around Earth (~27.3 days), a phenomenon known as tidal locking or synchronous rotation.

front_question: Detail the objective, procedure, observations, and conclusion for Activity 12.2 (To model solar and lunar eclipse shadow geometries using a torch and spheres.).
back_answer:
Materials: Torch (Sun), Large globe/ball (Earth), Small tennis ball (Moon), Darkened room
Procedure: Align torch light, small ball, and large globe in a straight line in a dark room. Observe shadow of small ball falling on large globe (Solar Eclipse simulation). Re-position large globe between torch and small ball to observe globe shadow covering small ball (Lunar Eclipse simulation).
Observation: In position 1, small ball blocks light, casting a shadow on globe. In position 2, large globe blocks light, submerging small ball in darkness.
Principle: Eclipses are natural shadow formations resulting from linear alignment of Sun, Earth, and Moon.

front_question: Explain how Earth's anti-clockwise rotation on its axis creates the apparent east-to-west movement of the Sun and stars.
back_answer: Just as a passenger on a clockwise merry-go-round sees surrounding trees spinning anti-clockwise, an observer on Earth rotating from West to East sees celestial bodies (Sun, stars) moving in the opposite direction from East to West.

front_question:
Case Scenario: An astronomer in Delhi observes a Total Solar Eclipse lasting 3 minutes, while an astronomer in Chennai sees only a Partial Solar Eclipse at the same time.
Question: Why did Delhi experience totality while Chennai experienced only a partial eclipse?
back_answer: Delhi was located within the narrow central umbral shadow cone cast by the Moon, blocking 100% of the Sun. Chennai was located in the broader penumbral shadow zone, where only part of the Sun was obstructed.

front_question:
Common Misconception: Believing seasons are caused by Earth moving closer to or farther from the Sun.
What is the scientifically correct fact?
back_answer: Seasons are caused by Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt during revolution, changing angle and duration of sunlight, NOT by distance variation from the Sun.
